questions.question: What is the objective of the agreement signed between the Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND) and the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) in April 2026?

options.text: To establish a unified cross-border tax evasion tracking system
To combat cyber fraud and financial crimes
To regulate the licensing of new digital payment startups in India
To monitor international stock market fluctuations for investment safety

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To combat cyber fraud and financial crimes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• In **April 2026**, the **Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND)** and the **Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C)** entered into a landmark agreement to strengthen the fight against **cyber-frauds** and **financial crimes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Enhanced Coordination:** The core focus of the MoU is to improve **information sharing** and coordination between the two agencies at the forefront of India’s fight against digital offenses.
 
• **Operational Support:** The collaboration assists in developing **operational information** to support **investigative agencies** in preventing financial crimes and undertaking **asset recovery**.
 
• **Fraud Detection:** It aims to establish **robust feedback mechanisms** for national-level **fraud detection protocols**.
 
• **Safeguarding Transactions:** The MoU focuses on protecting **digital transactions** and disseminating **red flag indicators** to financial institutions to prevent **cyber fraud**.
 
• **Signatories:** The agreement was signed by **Shri Amit Mohan Govil** (Director, FIU-IND) and **Shri Rajesh Kumar** (CEO, I4C).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **FIU-IND:** This is the central national agency responsible for analyzing and disseminating information related to **suspect financial transactions**, money laundering, and **terrorism financing**.
 
• **I4C:** It is an attached office of the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** that provides a framework for **Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs)** to handle cybercrime comprehensively.
 
• **I4C Platforms:** It manages platforms like the **National Cybercrime Reporting Portal (NCRP)**, Cyber-Police, and the **Suspect Registry** to combat online financial crimes.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• The MoU represents a **"whole of Government"** approach to address the **digital payment ecosystem's** transformation and its associated risks.
 
• The partnership aims to curb the misuse of **telecom** and **banking** resources through **real-time intelligence sharing**.

questions.question: The Abraham Accords, seen in recent international news, relate to:

options.text: Normalization of relations between Israel and Arab nations

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Normalization of relations between Israel and Arab nations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Abraham Accords** refer to a series of agreements brokered by the United States in **2020** between **Israel** and certain Arab nations, including the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)**, **Bahrain**, Sudan, and Morocco, to normalize diplomatic relations.

• The accords signify a shift in the **Middle East geopolitical landscape**, marking the first agreements between Israel and Arab nations since the peace treaties with Egypt in **1979** and Jordan in **1994**.

• The agreements focus on **establishing diplomatic ties**, fostering economic cooperation, and promoting peaceful coexistence between Israel and the participating nations.

• Under the Abraham Accords, the nations agreed to open **embassies**, facilitate direct flights, and strengthen ties in areas like **trade, tourism, security, and technology**.

• The accords are named after the patriarch **Abraham**, a figure revered in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam, symbolizing the shared historical and cultural heritage of the nations involved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Historical Context:**

• The Abraham Accords marked a significant departure from the traditional Arab stance on Israel, which often conditioned normalization on the resolution of the **Israeli-Palestinian conflict**.

• The agreements were signed in **September 2020** at the White House in Washington, D.C., under the mediation of then-U.S. President **Donald Trump**.

• The accords were viewed as a strategy to counter regional threats, particularly from **Iran**.

• **Participating Nations:**

• The **United Arab Emirates (UAE)** was the first Gulf Arab state to normalize relations with Israel under the Abraham Accords.

• **Bahrain** followed shortly, signing agreements to establish full diplomatic ties with Israel.

• **Sudan** and **Morocco** later joined the accords, normalizing relations with Israel in exchange for certain U.S. incentives.

• **Key Objectives:**

• Promote **peace and stability** in the Middle East.

• Enhance **economic cooperation** and foster trade relations among the signatory nations.

• Facilitate collaboration in **fields like technology, security, and healthcare**.

• **Outcomes and Impact:**

• The accords have facilitated **direct flights** between Israel and the participating nations and boosted tourism and cultural exchanges.

• They have also resulted in bilateral agreements in **technology, defense, and energy**.

• Critics argue that the accords sideline the **Palestinian cause**, as they do not address the core issues of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

• **Important Dates:**

• **August 13, 2020:** The UAE and Israel announced the normalization of relations, marking the first accord.

• **September 15, 2020:** The Abraham Accords were officially signed at the White House.

• **2020-2021:** Sudan and Morocco joined the accords under separate agreements.

</ul

questions.question: What is the significance of India's 10-year agreement with Iran regarding Chabahar Port?

options.text: It grants India operational control over the port
It allows India to export oil from Iran
It restricts trade between Iran and China
It merges Chabahar with Gwadar Port

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It grants India operational control over the port**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• In **May 2024**, India signed a landmark **10-year long-term agreement** with **Iran** to operate the **Shahid Beheshti terminal** at the **Chabahar Port**.

• The agreement was signed between **India Ports Global Limited (IPGL)** and the **Port and Maritime Organisation (PMO)** of Iran, granting India **operational control** over a key part of the port for the first time.

• The significance of this deal lies in its **strategic connectivity**; it provides India with a direct sea-land access route to **Afghanistan** and **Central Asian Republics**, effectively bypassing **Pakistan**.

• This long-term lease replaces the previous short-term annual renewals, providing **certainty and stability** for Indian investors and traders using the port.

• The deal is a major step in India's **geopolitical strategy** to counter the influence of the Chinese-managed **Gwadar Port** in Pakistan and to establish itself as a regional logistics hub.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Chabahar Port** is located in the **Sistan-Balochistan** province on Iran's energy-rich southern coast, situated at the mouth of the **Gulf of Oman**.

• It serves as a vital link in the **International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC)**, a multi-modal transport project connecting **India**, **Iran**, **Azerbaijan**, and **Russia** to **Europe**.

• As part of the agreement, India has committed to investing approximately **120 million USD** in equipping the terminal and has offered a **250 million USD** credit window for infrastructure development.

• The **Chabahar project** was initially conceptualized in **2003**, but gained significant momentum with a trilateral agreement between **India, Iran, and Afghanistan** in **2016**.
</ul

questions.question: Which malaria vaccine, co-developed by the University of Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, has been made significantly more accessible under a new agreement between Gavi and UNICEF?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**R21/Matrix-M.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, and UNICEF announced a new agreement to make the R21/Matrix-M malaria vaccine more accessible for global malaria prevention efforts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **R21/Matrix-M is the vaccine co-developed by the University of Oxford__ and the __Serum Institute of India__.**
 
• **It is one of only two malaria vaccines prequalified by WHO.**
 
• **The vaccine is safe, effective and capable of reducing malaria cases by around 75% in highly seasonal regions.**
 
• **The new Gavi–UNICEF agreement enhances affordability and supply access, especially for malaria-endemic countries.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **WHO-Prequalified Malaria Vaccines**__

 __
 
• **R21/Matrix-M** – Developed by University of Oxford + Serum Institute of India.
 
• **RTS,S/AS01** – Developed by GlaxoSmithKline (GSK), PATH and partners.
 
• Both are recommended by WHO for preventing malaria in children.
 
 
 
• **Effectiveness**__
 __
 
• Both vaccines reduce malaria cases by about **75%** when given seasonally in regions with high seasonal transmission.
 
• Such regions account for nearly **half of childhood malaria deaths** globally.
 
 
 
• **UNICEF and Vaccine Delivery**__
 __
 
• UNICEF is the world’s **largest vaccine buyer**, delivering around **3 billion doses** annually.
 
• Its procurement networks help ensure large-scale, equitable access to vaccines worldwide.
 
 
 
• **About Malaria**__
 __
 
• A vector-borne infectious disease caused by **Plasmodium parasites**.
 
• Transmitted through the bite of an infected **female Anopheles mosquito**.
 
• Symptoms include fever, chills, fatigue, and severe complications without treatment.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Gavi–UNICEF Agreement**__
 
 
• Boosts vaccine affordability and long-term supply security.
 
• Supports national immunisation programmes in malaria-endemic countries.
 
• Critical step in reducing child mortality and strengthening global malaria control strategies.

questions.question: The Uranium mining project in Sikar is being carried out in collaboration with DAE and which other directorate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**AMD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uranium mining project in Sikar:** The uranium mining project in the **Sikar district of Rajasthan** is a significant initiative undertaken to explore and extract uranium, a critical element used as fuel for nuclear power generation.
 
• This project is being executed in collaboration with the **Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)** and the **Atomic Minerals Directorate for Exploration and Research (AMD).** The AMD is directly responsible for conducting surveys, explorations, and feasibility studies for uranium mining. *Hence, option 2 is correct.*
 
• **Role of AMD:** The **Atomic Minerals Directorate** (AMD) functions under the **Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)**. It is tasked with identifying and assessing mineral resources required for India's nuclear power program, including uranium and thorium.
 
• While other organizations like **GSI (Geological Survey of India), MECL (Mineral Exploration Corporation Limited), and IBM (Indian Bureau of Mines)** have their respective roles in mineral exploration and mining, the specific task of uranium exploration and assessment is handled by the **AMD.**
 
• The **collaboration between DAE and AMD** ensures a focused approach to uranium exploration and contributes to India's strategic nuclear energy objectives. *Hence, option 2 is the most appropriate answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atomic Minerals Directorate for Exploration and Research (AMD):**

 
 
• The **AMD** was established in **1948** under the Department of Atomic Energy. It is headquartered in **Hyderabad**, India.
 
• The primary objective of AMD is to carry out detailed **exploration and assessment of uranium and other atomic minerals** such as thorium, zirconium, and rare earth elements in the country.
 
• It plays a key role in India's nuclear energy program by identifying and evaluating resources for nuclear fuel production.
 
 
 
• **Geological Survey of India (GSI):**
 
 
• The **GSI** was established in **1851**. It is primarily involved in conducting **geological surveys and studies** across India.
 
• Its role is to assess mineral resources and provide baseline geological data for exploration and development purposes, but it does not specialize in uranium exploration.
 
 
 
• **Mineral Exploration Corporation Limited (MECL):**
 
 
• The **MECL** was established in **1972** and is involved in detailed **exploration of various minerals**, including coal, lignite, and base metals.
 
• Although MECL supports mineral exploration activities, it is not primarily responsible for uranium exploration, which is the domain of AMD.
 
 
 
• **Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM):**
 
 
• The **IBM** was established in **1948** and functions under the Ministry of Mines. It is responsible for **regulating and promoting mineral development**, ensuring the conservation of minerals, and protecting the environment.
 
• IBM's role is more regulatory and administrative, focusing on the sustainable development of mineral resources, and it does not engage in uranium exploration or mining.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Uranium:**

 
 
• **Uranium** is a heavy metallic element used as **fuel in nuclear reactors**. It is essential for generating nuclear power and is also used in certain medical and defense applications.
 
• India's energy needs are growing, and uranium mining projects like the one in **Sikar** are crucial for supporting the country's nuclear power program.
 
 
 
• **Department of Atomic Energy (DAE):**
 
 
• The **DAE** is responsible for all nuclear-related activities in India, including nuclear power generation, research, and exploration of atomic minerals.
 
• It oversees organizations like **AMD, NPCIL (Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited), and BARC (Bhabha Atomic Research Centre).**

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between the **Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU)** and the **Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)** in April 2026?

options.text: To establish a unified export monitoring framework for the financial year
To upgrade Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Financing of Terrorism efforts
To conduct house-listing and housing census operations for pension holders
To negotiate nuclear enrichment rights under international law for financial entities

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To upgrade Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Financing of Terrorism efforts**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• In **April 2026**, the **Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU)** and the **Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)** signed a comprehensive **Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)** to boost the crackdown on money laundering and terror financing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Finance** stated that the MoU aims to enhance **information sharing** and **coordination** between the two agencies.
 
• The move is specifically focused on upgrading **Anti-Money Laundering (AML)** and **Combating Financing of Terrorism (CFT)** mechanisms.
 
• The partnership enables both agencies to undertake **outreach and training programmes** for **regulated or reporting entities**.
 
• The cooperation includes the identification and dissemination of **red flag indicators** for **suspicious transactions** to mitigate risks.
 
• It also involves the **assessment of Money Laundering and Terror Financing (ML/TF) risks** and vulnerabilities across relevant **financial sub-sectors**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

questions.question: Which of the following is the first country with which India signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Singapore**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 

• India signed its first **Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA)** with **Singapore** in **2005**. This agreement came into effect on **1st August 2005**. 

• The CEPA between India and Singapore aimed to strengthen **economic ties** by facilitating **trade in goods, services, and investments**. 

• It included provisions for **tariff reductions and eliminations** on goods traded between the two countries, making it easier for businesses to operate. 

• The agreement also promoted **investment flows** and encouraged cooperation in areas like **education, healthcare, and technology.** 

• Singapore has been one of India's **largest trading partners** in the ASEAN region, and the CEPA played a significant role in enhancing bilateral trade and economic relations. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
 

• **Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA):** 
 

• A CEPA is a kind of free trade agreement (FTA) that goes beyond conventional FTAs by including **trade in services, investment, intellectual property rights, competition, and dispute settlement**. 

• It aims to eliminate or reduce trade barriers such as tariffs and duties while promoting a more liberalized economic environment for businesses. 

• CEPAs often include provisions for **regulatory cooperation** and **mutual recognition agreements** in various sectors. 
 
 

• **India-Singapore Trade Relations:** 
 

• Singapore is a key player in the ASEAN region and serves as a **gateway to Southeast Asia** for Indian businesses. 

• In **2022-23**, the bilateral trade between India and Singapore was valued at approximately **USD 35 billion**, making Singapore one of India's most significant trading partners. 

• India exports goods like **petroleum products, pharmaceuticals, machinery, and textiles** to Singapore, while importing **electronics, chemicals, and machinery**. 
 
 

• **Other CEPAs Signed by India:** 
 

• After the success of the India-Singapore CEPA, India has signed other CEPAs, including with **South Korea (2010)**, **Japan (2011)**, and **UAE (2022)**. 

• These agreements aim to diversify India's trade partnerships and enhance its presence in global markets. 
 
 

• **Importance of CEPAs:** 
 

• They promote **economic growth** by reducing trade barriers and creating opportunities for businesses in partner countries. 

• CEPAs enhance **investment flows** and provide a framework for better regulatory cooperation. 

• They also help countries **integrate into global value chains**, boosting competitiveness in international markets.
